title: 4. Maslow's Hierarchy as a Character Motivation Map
use_cases: Use when mapping character development arcs based on psychological needs
Implement when designing character motivations to escalate dramatic tension
Configure when establishing a character's core drive at the start of a narrative
Use when identifying the vulnerability of a character by threatening a lower-tier need
content:
Abraham Maslow's hierarchy of needs (1943) is not just psychology — it is a direct map of escalating character motivation. Place your character at a specific level, then threaten the level below to create maximum dramatic conflict.

| Level | Need | Character Example | Conflict Created |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5. Physiological | Food, water, shelter | Katniss Everdeen | Survival drives all choices |
| 4. Safety | Security, stability | Frodo Baggins | Comfort vs duty |
| 3. Love/Belonging | Friendship, family, intimacy | Harry Potter | Orphan seeking family/belonging |
| 2. Esteem | Respect, recognition | Jay Gatsby | Obsessive status pursuit |
| 1. Self-Actualization | Purpose, full potential | Atticus Finch | Living by principle despite cost |

Reference: Abraham Maslow, "A Theory of Human Motivation," Psychological Review, 50(4), 370–396 (1943).
